name: Feature Engineering Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for feature engineering, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for feature engineering, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to feature engineering (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. When feature engineering decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
3. Before starting feature engineering work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. Prefer explicit, readable feature engineering solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
5. Validate feature engineering outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
6. Keep feature engineering changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
7. When multiple feature engineering strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
8. Prefer the simplest feature engineering approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
9. Surface known limitations of a chosen feature engineering approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
10. Measure before optimizing any feature engineering bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
11. State assumptions about feature engineering explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
12. When feature engineering guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated feature engineering concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop feature engineering edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not apply generic feature engineering advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting feature engineering assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new feature engineering abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about feature engineering over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
